questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify number of nucleophilic substitution reactions in the given reactions?
questions.solution:
Use the concept explained below on each of the reaction to identify the nucleophilic substitution reaction:

In a nucleophilic substitution reaction, the leaving group (nucleophile) is replaced by an electron rich compound (nucleophile). The whole molecular entity of which the electrophile and the leaving group are part is usually called the substrate. The nucleophile essentially attempts to replace the leaving group as the primary substituent in the reaction itself, as a part of another molecule.

Nuc: + R-LG → R-Nuc + LG:

The electron pair (:) from the nucleophile (Nuc) attacks the substrate (R-LG) forming a new bond, while the leaving group (LG) departs with an electron pair. The principal product in this case is R-Nucleophile. The nucleophile may be electrically neutral or negatively charged, whereas the substrate is typically neutral or positively charged.
An example of nucleophilic substitution is the hydrolysis of an alkyl bromide, R-Br, under basic conditions, where the attacking nucleophile is the OH− and the leaving group is Br−.
R-Br + OH− → R-OH + Br−

questions.q: How many of the following ethers CANNOT be prepared by Williamson's synthesis? ${\text{CH}}_{3}{\text{OCH}}_{2}{\text{CH}}_{3}, {\text{C}}_{6}{\text{H}}_{5}{\text{OCH}}_{3}, {( {\text{C}}_{6}{\text{H}}_{5} )}_{2}\text{O}\text{,}{( {\text{CH}}_{3} )}_{3}{\text{COCH}}_{3}, {( {\text{C}}_{2}{\text{H}}_{5} )}_{2}\text{O}, {( {\text{CH}}_{3} )}_{3}\text{C} - \text{O} - \text{C}{( {\text{CH}}_{3} )}_{3}$
questions.solution:
In Williamson's synthesis,
i. ${1}^{°}$ alkyl halide and ${3}^{°}$ alkoxide give best yield of corresponding ethers.
ii. In case of, ${3}^{°}$ alkyl halide, elimination competes over substitution and alkene is obtained as a product.
iii. Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution unless it is activated by the presence of electron withdrawing group. Thus, ${( {\text{C}}_{6}{\text{H}}_{5} )}_{2}\text{O}$ and ${( {\text{CH}}_{3} )}_{3}\text{C} - \text{O} - \text{C}{( {\text{CH}}_{3} )}_{3}$ cannot be prepared by Williamson's synthesis.

questions.q: Why is the oxidation of a primary alcohol witha mixture of sodium dichromate and sulphuric acid not a good method for the preparation of corresponding aldehyde?
options: The product will be the corresponding ketone
Any aldehyde produced will be oxidised further
The product will be an alkyl sulphonate, $R - {SO}_{3}H$ mixture of sodium dichromate and sulphuric acid will not oxidize a primary alcohol

questions.solution:

$PrimaryAlcohol\overset{\left[O\right]}{→}Aldehyde\overset{\left[O\right]}{→}Carboxylicacid$

So, any aldehyde produced will be oxidized further during the reaction.

questions.q: The number of alkenes (including stereoisomers) which can produce 2-butanol by the successive treatment of (i) ${B}_{2}{H}_{6}$ in tetrahydrofuran solvent and (ii) alkaline ${H}_{2}{O}_{2}$ solution is/are
questions.solution:
Structure of butan-2-ol is

$C{H}_{3} - \mathop{\mathop{C}_{|}H}_{OH} - C{H}_{2} - C{H}_{3}$

Now, the simple format of HBO (hydroboration oxidant) reaction is

$\text{R} - \text{CH} = {\text{CH}}_{2} + {\text{B}}_{2} {\text{H}}_{6} \overset{\text{THF}}{\to} {( \text{R} - {\text{CH}}_{2} {\text{CH}}_{2} )}_{3} \text{B}\overset{{\text{H}}_{2} {\text{O}}_{2} / \overset{-}{\text{O}} \text{H}}{\to} {\text{RCH}}_{2} \mathop{{\text{CH}}_{2}}_{\overset{|}{\text{OH}}}$

So, $C{H}_{3} - CH = CH - C{H}_{3}$ definitely an option as the mechanistic approach for the $B{H}_{3}$ addition is as



${( {\text{CH}}_{3} {\text{CH}}_{2} - {\text{CHCH}}_{3} )}_{3} \text{B}\overset{{\text{H}}_{2} {\text{O}}_{2} / \overset{-}{\text{O}} \text{H}}{\to} {\text{CH}}_{3} {\text{CH}}_{2} - \mathop{\mathop{\text{C}}_{|} \text{H}}_{\text{OH}} {\text{CH}}_{3}$

$2.R - \mathop{\mathop{C}_{| |}}_{O} - \mathop{\mathop{CH}_{|}}_{OH} - R$

$4.R - \mathop{\mathop{CH}_{|}}_{OH} - \mathop{\mathop{CH}_{|}}_{OH} - R\overset{HI{O}_{4}}{→}R - CH = O + O = HCR$
